bottom_line: In patients with heart failure, reduced LVEF, and intolerance to ACE inhibitors, losartan 150 mg daily versus 50 mg daily reduced death or admission for heart failure (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99).
implications: These data support that, in this ACE-inhibitor–intolerant heart failure population, losartan 150 mg daily yields a lower hazard of the composite of death or admission for heart failure than losartan 50 mg daily (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99) and a lower hazard of heart failure admission (HR 0.87, 0.76–0.98), while all-cause death was not significantly different (HR 0.94, 0.84–1.04). The results also show higher rates of renal impairment (454 vs 317), hypotension (203 vs 145), and hyperkalaemia (195 vs 131) with 150 mg, and they do not quantify benefit versus placebo.

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind trial comparing losartan 150 mg vs 50 mg daily in heart failure with reduced LVEF and ACE-inhibitor intolerance.
major_points.quote: This double-blind trial was undertaken in 255 sites in 30 countries. 3846 patients with heart failure of New York Heart Association class II–IV, left-ventricular ejection fraction 40% or less, and intolerance to angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitors were randomly assigned to losartan 150 mg (n=1927) or 50 mg daily (n=1919).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was the composite of death or admission for heart failure; analysis was intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was death or admission for heart failure. Analysis was by intention to treat.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint occurred less often with 150 mg vs 50 mg (HR 0.90) over median 4.7 years follow-up.
major_points.quote: With 4·7-year median follow-up in each group (IQR 3·7–5·5 for losartan 150 mg; 3·4–5·5 for losartan 50 mg), 828 (43%) patients in the 150 mg group versus 889 (46%) in the 50 mg group died or were admitted for heart failure (hazard ratio [HR] 0·90, 95% CI 0·82–0·99; p=0·027).

major_points.text: Heart failure admission was reduced with 150 mg vs 50 mg (HR 0.87), while all-cause death did not differ significantly.
major_points.quote: For the two primary endpoint components, 635 patients in the 150 mg group versus 665 in the 50 mg group died (HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·84–1·04; p=0·24), and 450 versus 503 patients were admitted for heart failure (0·87, 0·76–0·98; p=0·025).

major_points.text: Renal impairment, hypotension, and hyperkalaemia were more common with 150 mg than 50 mg, but discontinuations were not significantly increased.
major_points.quote: Renal impairment (n=454 vs 317), hypotension (203 vs 145), and hyperkalaemia (195 vs 131) were more common in the 150 mg group than in the 50 mg group, but these adverse events did not lead to signiﬁcantly more treatment discontinuations in the 150 mg group.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility criteria for patients were: age 18 years or older;
Eligibility criteria for patients were: age 18 years or older; symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association [NYHA] class II–IV);

inclusion_criteria.text: LVEF 40% or less, with stable cardiovascular medical therapy for at least 2 weeks.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility criteria for patients were: age 18 years or older; symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association [NYHA] class II–IV); LVEF 40% or less, with stable cardiovascular medical therapy for at least 2 weeks;

inclusion_criteria.text: Known intolerance to ACE inhibitors (defined by discontinuation due to specified adverse effects).
inclusion_criteria.quote: and known intolerance to ACE inhibitors. Intolerance was deﬁned as discontinuation of ACE-inhibitor treatment because of one or more of the following adverse eﬀects: cough, symptomatic hypotension, azotaemia, hyperkalaemia, taste disturbance, gastro-intestinal upset, or rash.

exclusion_criteria.quote: Exclusion criteria were: pregnancy or lactation;
Exclusion criteria were: pregnancy or lactation; known intolerance to ARBs;

exclusion_criteria.text: Systolic arterial blood pressure less than 90 mm Hg.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Exclusion criteria were: pregnancy or lactation; known intolerance to ARBs; systolic arterial blood pressure less than 90 mm Hg;

criticisms.text: The trial studied only ACE-inhibitor–intolerant patients.
criticisms.quote: Several limitations of HEAAL should be considered. We studied only patients who were intolerant to ACE inhibitors.

criticisms.text: Uncertainty whether findings would be reproduced in de novo patients versus those with known ACE inhibitor intolerance.
criticisms.quote: we cannot be certain whether our ﬁndings would be reproduced in patients being treated de novo, compared with those known to be intolerant of ACE inhibitors.

criticisms.text: Because losartan 50 mg daily was not tested against placebo, the magnitude of benefit of 150 mg cannot be directly estimated from this study.
criticisms.quote: Since the eﬀect of losartan 50 mg daily on outcomes related to heart failure has never been tested relative to placebo, direct estimations of the magnitude of beneﬁt of losartan 150 mg daily cannot be made from our results.

criticisms.text: The study cannot determine whether greater benefit might have been achievable by combining losartan with an ACE inhibitor rather than increasing dose.
criticisms.quote: we cannot establish whether greater beneﬁt might have been achievable by combining losartan with an ACE inhibitor, rather than further increasing the losartan dose.
